title: Understanding Over Origin: The Missing Friction

content_html:
A few days ago, I wrote "Understanding Over Origin" and it got alot of engagement and I'm really happy that it did because it means people took the time to read, understand my perspective and I get to engage with every one of them in the comments as well. Of course, not everyone agrees but that's irrevelant, the point is a healthy discussion between various perspective from different developers around the world.

But what I haven't told anyone is this: the more I engage, the more I realized something that I still do. I still write a lot of my code by hand and those are the parts I'm more proud of "

Not gatekeeping, not me being nostalgic or identity-defensive ( well, a little nostalgic ), that's me admitting the article I published was incomplete.

Some conversations don't end when the replies stop. My discussion with @darkwiiplayer was probably my favorite of all because more we talked, the more I found myself wrestling with an incomplete idea that refused to stay unfinished and this essay is the result.

What the Discussion Clarified

First, I need to thank the people who actually engaged with the core argument.

@unitbuilds gave his take that seams everything together and concludes the core idea of modern software enigeering: " If it can run a standardized benchmarking suite against competition, it's provable and reproducible. If that's good enough for a scientific discovery, it's good enough for programming.", they're not defending AI, they're saying with better standards available, we shouldn't choose to ignore them. He also pointed out something I'd missed, the burden of correctness has always been on the developer who signs off on the PR.

@madsendev who wrote the original article that sparked this whole discussion, showed genuine class. He came back, said the argument had "gone further," and proposed an idea that's stuck with me: what if AI-assisted projects included a standard where you quiz yourself on your own repository? Not to prove you didn't use AI, but to prove you actually understand what you built.

@komo hit on something important and i think it's my favorite takeaway from the discussion: "Maintenance receipts are much harder to fake." That single sentence reframes the entire debate. Tests. Bug fixes. Production incidents. Responding to issues. Refactoring. Every one of those leaves a trail of evidence that someone not only built the project but continues to understand, improve, and take responsibility for it. That's the kind of ownership that matters. It's earned over time, and it's far harder to fake than explaining code in an interview or claiming you wrote every line by hand.

I'm absolutely grateful that people gave in their thoughts but you can never have a good discussion without a pushback ⚔️

the pushback's always my favorite part of any technical discussion.

The Challenge That Made Me Think

@darkwiiplayer showed up and said something like: "Training AI on stolen code without consent is theft. Everything built with AI carries that theft in its DNA. You're overlooking this."

She wasn't being rhetorical, she was actually making a philosophical point about training data, consent, and what "learning" means when it's done at scale without permission.

We went back and forth. I argued that training data and generated output aren't automatically equivalent to copying and she countered that if you removed all stolen code from training data, the models wouldn't exist as they do. Which is... probably true? And that matters.

I don't think it invalidates the engineering argument. But it does mean the conversation has two layers:

  1. The technical layer: is the work maintained, understood, and good?
  2. The ethical layer: how should we feel about tools built on potentially non-consensual training data?

Most people in that thread were debating layer 1 and she dragged me down to layer 2 into the conversation. Both are real. Neither invalidates the other.

But it also made me realize my original article didn't address why handwritten code felt different to me because honestly? it does.

The Real Tension

The argument I made: origin doesn't determine quality. Understanding, testing, maintainability, accountability, that's what matters.

My own experience reflects that. I started writing code around 2018, and back then the only AI most of us could name was Sophia, the humanoid robot from Hong Kong. I learned the traditional way: by writing everything myself. Even today, when I write code by hand, I understand it differently. More deeply. I notice edge cases I might have overlooked if I'd generated the first draft with AI. And when I'm done, I'm genuinely more proud of what I've built.

These aren't compatible statements if you think about them too hard.

Either:

  1. My pride is just ego (origin bias)
  2. Handwritten code actually is better (proving the gatekeepers right)
  3. Both are true, but for reasons I didn't examine

@fromzerotoship helped me see option 3 clearly. They're not a developer but they've shipped 20+ working internal tools using AI. A hospital runs them. By my standards, they'd "fail" the understanding test, there are parts of their system they couldn't explain line-by-line.

But then they said something that shifted everything: "Demonstrable behavior under deliberate failure is another form of earning trust, and it's the only one available to me. It's also harder to fake."

Plant defects, watch the guards catch them, restore the guards and watch them go green and then deploy and check the URLs a few seconds later.

they demonstrate that they can keep it alive.

And that made me realize the real distinction wasn't about who typed the code. It was about friction.

The Friction Actually Matters

In my earlier piece I wrote a few weeks ago, I described not being able to write some logic from scratch despite reviewing it perfectly, that wasn't just skill loss. It was proof that I'd skipped the friction that builds actual understanding.

When I write code by hand, I encounter problems in real-time.

I hit a wall. My approach doesn't work. I refactor. I discover the problem space through constraint and failure. I make decisions about decisions, not just typing, but choosing between paths I've actually explored. this is the learning path that I unknowingly go through whenever I write code by hand and Wii reminded me of this.

When I use AI, I describe what I want. I get options. I pick the one that looks right. I'm curating, not exploring.

Both can produce good code. But the path to understanding is fundamentally different.

With handwritten code: friction, insight, better next decisions

With AI-assisted: selection, implementation, validation

The friction is the learning mechanism.

So when I say I'm more proud of handwritten code? I'm not being romantic about suffering. I'm noting that the code I'm proudest of is the code I fought for, and handwriting forces the fight.

But Here's the Problem With That Logic

If friction is the mechanism, then the type of friction matters more than who did the typing.

You could write AI-assisted code where you:

  • Fight with the prompt
  • Critique every generated option
  • Refactor aggressively
  • Hit walls and redesign

That has friction and it also builds understanding.

Conversely, you could hand-write code where you:

  • Autopilot through a familiar pattern
  • Never question assumptions
  • Copy-paste from Stack Overflow
  • Never understand why it works

That has no friction and it builds nothing.

So the honest version of my position isn't "handwritten code is better." It's: "friction builds understanding, and handwriting tends to create friction because you're forced to think through every line."

But that's a contingent truth, not an absolute one.

The Uncomfortable Realization

The critics ( gatekeepers, but we'll stick with this from now on ) were partially right and I was too generous in my original position.

Not about the gatekeeping itself, no, that's still wrong. But about the tendency: AI does make it easier to produce low-understanding code. Not because AI is bad, but because removing friction is literally what AI does, and friction is what builds understanding.

The answer isn't "use less AI" or "never use AI." It's "if you use AI to skip engagement with the problem, whether that's the code, the failure modes, or the maintenance, you build worse systems.

That applies to humans too but humans have an inherent friction cost, we get bored, we hate typing, we make mistakes. That friction is annoying, but it forces us to stay engaged.

So What Changed?

Nothing about the original argument was wrong. But I was treating "understanding + accountability" as if they were just checkboxes you could verify at the end.

They're not.

Understanding isn't a property you can inspect, it's a process and that process requires friction. Real engagement with the problem. Mistakes you learn from.

The reason I'm prouder of handwritten code is because I earned the understanding in a way that's harder to fake.

Does that mean every line should be handwritten? No. Boilerplate is boilerplate. Some friction is just noise.

But the core logic? The architecture decisions? The places where "understanding this code" actually matters? Yeah, I want to have fought for that.

And I want the same from anyone shipping code that matters.

The Uncomfortable Middle Ground

Here's where I land:

To the critics: You're using the wrong filter. "AI or no AI" doesn't tell you anything but you're accidentally right that there's something real to be concerned about, it's the laziness that AI enables, not the tool itself.

To AI enthusiasts: Yeah, your tooling is amazing. But it's worth asking whether you're using it to think better or think less. Those feel the same until you try to maintain the code six months later.

To myself: The pride I feel in handwritten code isn't ego, It's legitimate. every line that I typed out isn't some sort of magical unicorn mythological Godly line but it's the friction that comes with it, the learning I build that comes with it.

Sometimes the answer requires admitting you skipped and sometimes that's fine for routine work. But if you're building something that matters, you should want to have fought for it.

Choose Where You Fight

I still write a lot of code by hand. I still use AI every day. Those aren't contradictions anymore.

The original article was right: origin doesn't determine quality. What it missed is that understanding isn't a checkbox you tick at the end. It's something you earn through friction. Handwriting tends to create that friction. AI tends to remove it. Neither is inherently good or bad. Both are choices about how you engage with the problem.

So I'm not asking "Did you use AI?" anymore.

I'm asking: Did you fight for the parts that matter?

And if the tool answered that for you, you'll find out the next time something breaks.

blocks.html_en: We went back and forth. I argued that training data and generated output aren't automatically equivalent to copying and she countered that if you removed all stolen code from training data, the models wouldn't exist as they do. Which is... probably true? And that matters.

sentences.en: We went back and forth.
sentences.zh: 我们来来回回。

sentences.en: I argued that training data and generated output aren't automatically equivalent to copying and she countered that if you removed all stolen code from training data, the models wouldn't exist as they do.
sentences.zh: 我认为训练数据和生成的输出并不自动等同于复制，她反驳说，如果你从训练数据中删除所有被盗的代码，模型就不会像现在这样存在。

sentences.en: Which is...
sentences.zh: 这是...

sentences.en: probably true?
sentences.zh: 也许是真的？

sentences.en: And that matters.
sentences.zh: 这很重要。

blocks.html_en: I don't think it invalidates the engineering argument. But it does mean the conversation has two layers:

sentences.en: I don't think it invalidates the engineering argument.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这会使工程​​论点无效。

sentences.en: But it does mean the conversation has two layers:
sentences.zh: 但这确实意味着对话有两个层次：

blocks.html_en: • The technical layer: is the work maintained, understood, and good?

sentences.en: The technical layer: is the work maintained, understood, and good?
sentences.zh: 技术层：工作是否得到维护、理解和良好？

blocks.html_en: • The ethical layer: how should we feel about tools built on potentially non-consensual training data?

sentences.en: The ethical layer: how should we feel about tools built on potentially non-consensual training data?
sentences.zh: 道德层面：我们应该如何看待基于潜在非共识训练数据构建的工具？

blocks.html_en: Most people in that thread were debating layer 1 and she dragged me down to layer 2 into the conversation. Both are real. Neither invalidates the other.

sentences.en: Most people in that thread were debating layer 1 and she dragged me down to layer 2 into the conversation.
sentences.zh: 该线程中的大多数人都在讨论第一层，她将我拉到第二层进行对话。

sentences.en: Both are real.
sentences.zh: 两者都是真实的。

sentences.en: Neither invalidates the other.
sentences.zh: 两者都不会使对方无效。

blocks.html_en: But it also made me realize my original article didn't address why handwritten code felt different to me because honestly? it does.

sentences.en: But it also made me realize my original article didn't address why handwritten code felt different to me because honestly?
sentences.zh: 但这也让我意识到我原来的文章并没有解决为什么手写代码对我来说感觉不同，因为老实说？

sentences.en: it does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

blocks.html_en: The Real Tension

sentences.en: The Real Tension
sentences.zh: 真正的紧张局势

blocks.html_en: The argument I made: origin doesn't determine quality. Understanding, testing, maintainability, accountability, that's what matters.

sentences.en: The argument I made: origin doesn't determine quality.
sentences.zh: 我提出的论点是：产地并不决定质量。

sentences.en: Understanding, testing, maintainability, accountability, that's what matters.
sentences.zh: 理解、测试、可维护性、责任感，这才是重要的。

blocks.html_en: My own experience reflects that. I started writing code around 2018, and back then the only AI most of us could name was Sophia, the humanoid robot from Hong Kong. I learned the traditional way: by writing everything myself. Even today, when I write code by hand, I understand it differently. More deeply. I notice edge cases I might have overlooked if I'd generated the first draft with AI. And when I'm done, I'm genuinely more proud of what I've built.

sentences.en: My own experience reflects that.
sentences.zh: 我自己的经历也反映了这一点。

sentences.en: I started writing code around 2018, and back then the only AI most of us could name was Sophia, the humanoid robot from Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 我在 2018 年左右开始编写代码，当时我们大多数人唯一能说出名字的人工智能是来自香港的人形机器人 Sophia。

sentences.en: I learned the traditional way: by writing everything myself.
sentences.zh: 我以传统的方式学习：自己写所有东西。

sentences.en: Even today, when I write code by hand, I understand it differently.
sentences.zh: 即使在今天，当我手工编写代码时，我对它的理解也有所不同。

sentences.en: More deeply.
sentences.zh: 更深入一点。

sentences.en: I notice edge cases I might have overlooked if I'd generated the first draft with AI.
sentences.zh: 我注意到如果我用人工智能生成初稿，我可能会忽略一些边缘情况。

sentences.en: And when I'm done, I'm genuinely more proud of what I've built.
sentences.zh: 当我完成后，我真的为我所构建的东西感到更加自豪。

blocks.html_en: These aren't compatible statements if you think about them too hard.

sentences.en: These aren't compatible statements if you think about them too hard.
sentences.zh: 如果你想得太仔细的话，这些说法就不兼容。

blocks.html_en: Either:

sentences.en: Either:
sentences.zh: 任何一个：

blocks.html_en: • My pride is just ego (origin bias)

sentences.en: My pride is just ego (origin bias)
sentences.zh: 我的骄傲只是自我（出身偏见）

blocks.html_en: • Handwritten code actually is better (proving the gatekeepers right)

sentences.en: Handwritten code actually is better (proving the gatekeepers right)
sentences.zh: 手写代码实际上更好（证明看门人是正确的）

blocks.html_en: • Both are true, but for reasons I didn't examine

sentences.en: Both are true, but for reasons I didn't examine
sentences.zh: 两者都是正确的，但由于我没有检查的原因

blocks.html_en: @fromzerotoship helped me see option 3 clearly. They're not a developer but they've shipped 20+ working internal tools using AI. A hospital runs them. By my standards, they'd "fail" the understanding test, there are parts of their system they couldn't explain line-by-line.

sentences.en: @fromzerotoship helped me see option 3 clearly.
sentences.zh: @fromzerotoship 帮助我清楚地看到了选项 3。

sentences.en: They're not a developer but they've shipped 20+ working internal tools using AI.
sentences.zh: 他们不是开发人员，但他们已经使用 AI 发布了 20 多个可用的内部工具。

sentences.en: A hospital runs them.
sentences.zh: 一家医院经营它们。

sentences.en: By my standards, they'd "fail" the understanding test, there are parts of their system they couldn't explain line-by-line.
sentences.zh: 按照我的标准，他们的理解测试“未通过”，他们系统的某些部分无法逐行解释。

blocks.html_en: But then they said something that shifted everything: "Demonstrable behavior under deliberate failure is another form of earning trust, and it's the only one available to me. It's also harder to fake."

sentences.en: But then they said something that shifted everything: "Demonstrable behavior under deliberate failure is another form of earning trust, and it's the only one available to me.
sentences.zh: 但随后他们说了一句话，改变了一切：“在故意失败的情况下表现出来的行为是赢得信任的另一种形式，这是我唯一可以采用的形式。

sentences.en: It's also harder to fake."
sentences.zh: 造假也更难。”

blocks.html_en: Plant defects, watch the guards catch them, restore the guards and watch them go green and then deploy and check the URLs a few seconds later.

sentences.en: Plant defects, watch the guards catch them, restore the guards and watch them go green and then deploy and check the URLs a few seconds later.
sentences.zh: 植入缺陷，观察守卫捕获它们，恢复守卫并观察它们变绿，然后在几秒钟后部署并检查 URL。

blocks.html_en: they demonstrate that they can keep it alive.

sentences.en: they demonstrate that they can keep it alive.
sentences.zh: 他们证明他们可以保持它的活力。

blocks.html_en: And that made me realize the real distinction wasn't about who typed the code. It was about friction.

sentences.en: And that made me realize the real distinction wasn't about who typed the code.
sentences.zh: 这让我意识到真正的区别不在于谁输入了代码。

sentences.en: It was about friction.
sentences.zh: 这是关于摩擦的。

blocks.html_en: The Friction Actually Matters

sentences.en: The Friction Actually Matters
sentences.zh: 摩擦力实际上很重要

blocks.html_en: In my earlier piece I wrote a few weeks ago, I described not being able to write some logic from scratch despite reviewing it perfectly, that wasn't just skill loss. It was proof that I'd skipped the friction that builds actual understanding.

sentences.en: In my earlier piece I wrote a few weeks ago, I described not being able to write some logic from scratch despite reviewing it perfectly, that wasn't just skill loss.
sentences.zh: 在我几周前写的早期文章中，我描述了尽管完美地审查了一些逻辑，但仍无法从头开始编写一些逻辑，这不仅仅是技能损失。

sentences.en: It was proof that I'd skipped the friction that builds actual understanding.
sentences.zh: 这证明我跳过了建立实际理解的摩擦。

blocks.html_en: When I write code by hand, I encounter problems in real-time.

sentences.en: When I write code by hand, I encounter problems in real-time.
sentences.zh: 当我手工编写代码时，我会实时遇到问题。

blocks.html_en: I hit a wall. My approach doesn't work. I refactor. I discover the problem space through constraint and failure. I make decisions about decisions, not just typing, but choosing between paths I've actually explored. this is the learning path that I unknowingly go through whenever I write code by hand and Wii reminded me of this.

sentences.en: I hit a wall.
sentences.zh: 我碰壁了。

sentences.en: My approach doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 我的方法行不通。

sentences.en: I refactor.
sentences.zh: 我重构。

sentences.en: I discover the problem space through constraint and failure.
sentences.zh: 我通过约束和失败发现问题空间。

sentences.en: I make decisions about decisions, not just typing, but choosing between paths I've actually explored.
sentences.zh: 我做出关于决定的决定，不仅仅是打字，而是在我实际探索过的路径之间进行选择。

sentences.en: this is the learning path that I unknowingly go through whenever I write code by hand and Wii reminded me of this.
sentences.zh: 这就是我每次手写代码时不知不觉地经历的学习路径，Wii 提醒了我这一点。

blocks.html_en: When I use AI, I describe what I want. I get options. I pick the one that looks right. I'm curating, not exploring.

sentences.en: When I use AI, I describe what I want.
sentences.zh: 当我使用人工智能时，我会描述我想要什么。

sentences.en: I get options.
sentences.zh: 我有选择。

sentences.en: I pick the one that looks right.
sentences.zh: 我选一个看起来合适的。

sentences.en: I'm curating, not exploring.
sentences.zh: 我是在策划，而不是在探索。

blocks.html_en: Both can produce good code. But the path to understanding is fundamentally different.

sentences.en: Both can produce good code.
sentences.zh: 两者都可以产生好的代码。

sentences.en: But the path to understanding is fundamentally different.
sentences.zh: 但理解的道路却有着根本的不同。

blocks.html_en: With handwritten code: friction, insight, better next decisions

sentences.en: With handwritten code: friction, insight, better next decisions
sentences.zh: 使用手写代码：摩擦、洞察力、更好的下一步决策

blocks.html_en: With AI-assisted: selection, implementation, validation

sentences.en: With AI-assisted: selection, implementation, validation
sentences.zh: 人工智能辅助：选择、实施、验证

blocks.html_en: The friction is the learning mechanism.

sentences.en: The friction is the learning mechanism.
sentences.zh: 摩擦就是学习机制。

blocks.html_en: So when I say I'm more proud of handwritten code? I'm not being romantic about suffering. I'm noting that the code I'm proudest of is the code I fought for, and handwriting forces the fight.

sentences.en: So when I say I'm more proud of handwritten code?
sentences.zh: 那么当我说我对手写代码更感到自豪时？

sentences.en: I'm not being romantic about suffering.
sentences.zh: 我对苦难并不浪漫。

sentences.en: I'm noting that the code I'm proudest of is the code I fought for, and handwriting forces the fight.
sentences.zh: 我注意到我最引以为豪的代码是我为之奋斗的代码，而手写则迫使我去奋斗。

blocks.html_en: But Here's the Problem With That Logic

sentences.en: But Here's the Problem With That Logic
sentences.zh: 但这就是这个逻辑的问题

blocks.html_en: If friction is the mechanism, then the type of friction matters more than who did the typing.

sentences.en: If friction is the mechanism, then the type of friction matters more than who did the typing.
sentences.zh: 如果摩擦是一种机制，那么摩擦的类型比谁打字更重要。

blocks.html_en: You could write AI-assisted code where you:

sentences.en: You could write AI-assisted code where you:
sentences.zh: 您可以在以下位置编写人工智能辅助代码：

blocks.html_en: • Fight with the prompt

sentences.en: Fight with the prompt
sentences.zh: 根据提示进行战斗

blocks.html_en: • Critique every generated option

sentences.en: Critique every generated option
sentences.zh: 批评每个生成的选项

blocks.html_en: • Refactor aggressively

sentences.en: Refactor aggressively
sentences.zh: 积极重构

blocks.html_en: • Hit walls and redesign

sentences.en: Hit walls and redesign
sentences.zh: 撞墙并重新设计

blocks.html_en: That has friction and it also builds understanding.

sentences.en: That has friction and it also builds understanding.
sentences.zh: 这会产生摩擦，也会建立理解。

blocks.html_en: Conversely, you could hand-write code where you:

sentences.en: Conversely, you could hand-write code where you:
sentences.zh: 相反，您可以手写代码，其中：

blocks.html_en: • Autopilot through a familiar pattern

sentences.en: Autopilot through a familiar pattern
sentences.zh: 通过熟悉的模式自动驾驶

blocks.html_en: • Never question assumptions

sentences.en: Never question assumptions
sentences.zh: 永远不要质疑假设

blocks.html_en: • Copy-paste from Stack Overflow

sentences.en: Copy-paste from Stack Overflow
sentences.zh: 从 Stack Overflow 复制粘贴

blocks.html_en: • Never understand why it works

sentences.en: Never understand why it works
sentences.zh: 永远不明白为什么它有效

blocks.html_en: That has no friction and it builds nothing.

sentences.en: That has no friction and it builds nothing.
sentences.zh: 这没有摩擦力，也不会建造任何东西。

blocks.html_en: So the honest version of my position isn't "handwritten code is better." It's: "friction builds understanding, and handwriting tends to create friction because you're forced to think through every line."

sentences.en: So the honest version of my position isn't "handwritten code is better."
sentences.zh: 所以我的立场的诚实版本并不是“手写代码更好”。

sentences.en: It's: "friction builds understanding, and handwriting tends to create friction because you're forced to think through every line."
sentences.zh: 它是：“摩擦可以建立理解，而手写往往会产生摩擦，因为你被迫思考每一行。”

blocks.html_en: But that's a contingent truth, not an absolute one.

sentences.en: But that's a contingent truth, not an absolute one.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个偶然的事实，而不是绝对的事实。

blocks.html_en: The Uncomfortable Realization

sentences.en: The Uncomfortable Realization
sentences.zh: 令人不安的认识

blocks.html_en: The critics ( gatekeepers, but we'll stick with this from now on ) were partially right and I was too generous in my original position.

sentences.en: The critics ( gatekeepers, but we'll stick with this from now on ) were partially right and I was too generous in my original position.
sentences.zh: 批评者（守门人，但从现在开始我们将坚持这一点）部分正确，而我在原来的立场上过于慷慨。

blocks.html_en: Not about the gatekeeping itself, no, that's still wrong. But about the tendency: AI does make it easier to produce low-understanding code. Not because AI is bad, but because removing friction is literally what AI does, and friction is what builds understanding.

sentences.en: Not about the gatekeeping itself, no, that's still wrong.
sentences.zh: 不是关于守门本身，不，这仍然是错误的。

sentences.en: But about the tendency: AI does make it easier to produce low-understanding code.
sentences.zh: 但关于趋势：人工智能确实使生成低理解性代码变得更容易。

sentences.en: Not because AI is bad, but because removing friction is literally what AI does, and friction is what builds understanding.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为人工智能不好，而是因为消除摩擦正是人工智能所做的事情，而摩擦正是建立理解的基础。

blocks.html_en: The answer isn't "use less AI" or "never use AI." It's "if you use AI to skip engagement with the problem, whether that's the code, the failure modes, or the maintenance, you build worse systems.

sentences.en: The answer isn't "use less AI" or "never use AI."
sentences.zh: 答案不是“少用人工智能”或“从不使用人工智能”。

sentences.en: It's "if you use AI to skip engagement with the problem, whether that's the code, the failure modes, or the maintenance, you build worse systems.
sentences.zh: “如果你使用人工智能来跳过解决问题的过程，无论是代码、故障模式还是维护，你都会构建出更糟糕的系统。

blocks.html_en: That applies to humans too but humans have an inherent friction cost, we get bored, we hate typing, we make mistakes. That friction is annoying, but it forces us to stay engaged.

sentences.en: That applies to humans too but humans have an inherent friction cost, we get bored, we hate typing, we make mistakes.
sentences.zh: 这也适用于人类，但人类有固有的摩擦成本，我​​们会感到无聊，我们讨厌打字，我们会犯错误。

sentences.en: That friction is annoying, but it forces us to stay engaged.
sentences.zh: 这种摩擦很烦人，但它迫使我们保持参与。

blocks.html_en: So What Changed?

sentences.en: So What Changed?
sentences.zh: 那么什么改变了？

blocks.html_en: Nothing about the original argument was wrong. But I was treating "understanding + accountability" as if they were just checkboxes you could verify at the end.

sentences.en: Nothing about the original argument was wrong.
sentences.zh: 原来的论点没有任何错误。

sentences.en: But I was treating "understanding + accountability" as if they were just checkboxes you could verify at the end.
sentences.zh: 但我将“理解+责任”视为你可以在最后验证的复选框。

blocks.html_en: They're not.

sentences.en: They're not.
sentences.zh: 他们不是。

blocks.html_en: Understanding isn't a property you can inspect, it's a process and that process requires friction. Real engagement with the problem. Mistakes you learn from.

sentences.en: Understanding isn't a property you can inspect, it's a process and that process requires friction.
sentences.zh: 理解不是一种可以检查的财产，而是一个过程，而这个过程需要摩擦。

sentences.en: Real engagement with the problem.
sentences.zh: 真正参与解决问题。

sentences.en: Mistakes you learn from.
sentences.zh: 你从中吸取教训的错误。

blocks.html_en: The reason I'm prouder of handwritten code is because I earned the understanding in a way that's harder to fake.

sentences.en: The reason I'm prouder of handwritten code is because I earned the understanding in a way that's harder to fake.
sentences.zh: 我对手写代码感到更加自豪的原因是因为我以一种难以伪造的方式获得了理解。

blocks.html_en: Does that mean every line should be handwritten? No. Boilerplate is boilerplate. Some friction is just noise.

sentences.en: Does that mean every line should be handwritten?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着每一行都应该手写？

sentences.en: No. Boilerplate is boilerplate.
sentences.zh: 不，样板就是样板。

sentences.en: Some friction is just noise.
sentences.zh: 有些摩擦只是噪音。

blocks.html_en: But the core logic? The architecture decisions? The places where "understanding this code" actually matters? Yeah, I want to have fought for that.

sentences.en: But the core logic?
sentences.zh: 但核心逻辑是什么？

sentences.en: The architecture decisions?
sentences.zh: 架构决策？

sentences.en: The places where "understanding this code" actually matters?
sentences.zh: “理解这段代码”真正重要的地方是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, I want to have fought for that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想为此而奋斗。

blocks.html_en: And I want the same from anyone shipping code that matters.

sentences.en: And I want the same from anyone shipping code that matters.
sentences.zh: 我希望任何重要的运输代码也能得到同样的结果。

blocks.html_en: The Uncomfortable Middle Ground

sentences.en: The Uncomfortable Middle Ground
sentences.zh: 不舒服的中间地带

blocks.html_en: Here's where I land:

sentences.en: Here's where I land:
sentences.zh: 这是我着陆的地方：

blocks.html_en: To the critics: You're using the wrong filter. "AI or no AI" doesn't tell you anything but you're accidentally right that there's something real to be concerned about, it's the laziness that AI enables, not the tool itself.

sentences.en: To the critics: You're using the wrong filter.
sentences.zh: 对于批评者：您使用了错误的过滤器。

sentences.en: "AI or no AI" doesn't tell you anything but you're accidentally right that there's something real to be concerned about, it's the laziness that AI enables, not the tool itself.
sentences.zh: “人工智能或没有人工智能”并不能告诉你任何事情，但你意外地正确地知道有一些真正值得关注的事情，这是人工智能带来的懒惰，而不是工具本身。

blocks.html_en: To AI enthusiasts: Yeah, your tooling is amazing. But it's worth asking whether you're using it to think better or think less. Those feel the same until you try to maintain the code six months later.

sentences.en: To AI enthusiasts: Yeah, your tooling is amazing.
sentences.zh: 致人工智能爱好者：是的，你们的工具太棒了。

sentences.en: But it's worth asking whether you're using it to think better or think less.
sentences.zh: 但值得一问的是，你是用它来更好地思考还是更少地思考。

sentences.en: Those feel the same until you try to maintain the code six months later.
sentences.zh: 直到六个月后您尝试维护代码之前，这些感觉都是一样的。

blocks.html_en: To myself: The pride I feel in handwritten code isn't ego, It's legitimate. every line that I typed out isn't some sort of magical unicorn mythological Godly line but it's the friction that comes with it, the learning I build that comes with it.

sentences.en: To myself: The pride I feel in handwritten code isn't ego, It's legitimate.
sentences.zh: 对我自己来说：我对手写代码的自豪感不是自我，而是合理的。

sentences.en: every line that I typed out isn't some sort of magical unicorn mythological Godly line but it's the friction that comes with it, the learning I build that comes with it.
sentences.zh: 我打出的每一行并不是某种神奇的独角兽神话中的神行，而是随之而来的摩擦，我所建立的学习。

blocks.html_en: Sometimes the answer requires admitting you skipped and sometimes that's fine for routine work. But if you're building something that matters, you should want to have fought for it.

sentences.en: Sometimes the answer requires admitting you skipped and sometimes that's fine for routine work.
sentences.zh: 有时答案需要承认您跳过了，有时这对于日常工作来说很好。

sentences.en: But if you're building something that matters, you should want to have fought for it.
sentences.zh: 但如果你正在构建一些重要的东西，你应该愿意为之奋斗。

blocks.html_en: Choose Where You Fight

sentences.en: Choose Where You Fight
sentences.zh: 选择战斗地点

content_html_zh:
几天前，我写了《理解起源》，它得到了很多人的参与，我真的很高兴它做到了，因为这意味着人们花时间阅读、理解我的观点，而我也可以在评论中与他们每一个人互动。 当然，并不是每个人都同意，但这并不重要，重点是来自世界各地不同开发人员的不同观点之间的健康讨论。

但我没有告诉任何人的是：我参与得越多，我就越意识到我仍在做的事情。 我仍然手工编写很多代码，这些是我更引以为傲的部分”

不是把关，不是我怀旧或身份防御（好吧，有点怀旧），这是我承认我发表的文章不完整。

当回复停止时，有些对话并没有结束。 我与@darkwiiplayer 的讨论可能是我最喜欢的，因为我们讨论得越多，我就越发现自己在与一个不完整的想法作斗争，拒绝保持未完成状态，这篇文章就是结果。

讨论澄清了什么

首先，我要感谢那些真正参与核心论点的人。

@unitbuilds 给出了他的观点，将所有内容结合在一起，并总结了现代软件工程的核心思想：“如果它可以运行标准化的基准测试套件来对抗竞争，那么它就是可证明和可重复的。 如果这对于科学发现来说足够好，那么对于编程来说也足够好。”，他们并不是在捍卫人工智能，而是说有了更好的标准，我们不应该选择忽视它们。 他还指出了我错过的一些事情，正确性的责任始终落在签署 PR 的开发人员身上。

@madsendev 撰写了引发整个讨论的原始文章，表现出了真正的水平。 他回来说，争论已经“走得更远”，并提出了一个让我印象深刻的想法：如果人工智能辅助项目包含一个标准，让你在自己的存储库上自我测验，会怎么样？ 不是为了证明你没有使用人工智能，而是为了证明你真正理解你所构建的东西。

@komo 发现了一些重要的东西，我认为这是我在讨论中最喜欢的收获：“维护收据更难伪造。” 这一句话重新定义了整个辩论。 测试。 错误修复。 生产事故。 回应问题。 重构。 每一个都留下了证据，证明有人不仅建造了这个项目，而且还在继续理解、改进它并承担责任。 这才是重要的所有权。 它是随着时间的推移而获得的，而且比在采访中解释代码或声称你手写每一行要困难得多。

我非常感谢人们提出自己的想法，但如果没有阻力，你永远不可能进行良好的讨论⚔️

在任何技术讨论中，阻力始终是我最喜欢的部分。

让我思考的挑战

@darkwiiplayer 出现并说了这样的话：“未经同意用窃取的代码训练人工智能就是盗窃。 所有用人工智能构建的东西都带着这种盗窃的基因。 你忽视了这一点。”

她并不是在说教，她实际上是在表达一个关于训练数据、同意以及未经许可大规模学习时“学习”意味着什么的哲学观点。

我们来来回回。 我认为训练数据和生成的输出并不自动等同于复制，她反驳说，如果你从训练数据中删除所有被盗的代码，模型就不会像现在这样存在。 这是... 也许是真的？ 这很重要。

我不认为这会使工程​​论点无效。 但这确实意味着对话有两个层次：

  1. 技术层：工作是否得到维护、理解和良好？
  2. 道德层面：我们应该如何看待基于潜在非共识训练数据构建的工具？

该线程中的大多数人都在讨论第一层，她将我拉到第二层进行对话。 两者都是真实的。 两者都不会使对方无效。

但这也让我意识到我原来的文章并没有解决为什么手写代码对我来说感觉不同，因为老实说？ 确实如此。

真正的紧张局势

我提出的论点是：产地并不决定质量。 理解、测试、可维护性、责任感，这才是重要的。

我自己的经历也反映了这一点。 我在 2018 年左右开始编写代码，当时我们大多数人唯一能说出名字的人工智能是来自香港的人形机器人 Sophia。 我以传统的方式学习：自己写所有东西。 即使在今天，当我手工编写代码时，我对它的理解也有所不同。 更深入一点。 我注意到如果我用人工智能生成初稿，我可能会忽略一些边缘情况。 当我完成后，我真的为我所构建的东西感到更加自豪。

如果你想得太仔细的话，这些说法就不兼容。

任何一个：

  1. 我的骄傲只是自我（出身偏见）
  2. 手写代码实际上更好（证明看门人是正确的）
  3. 两者都是正确的，但由于我没有检查的原因

@fromzerotoship 帮助我清楚地看到了选项 3。 他们不是开发人员，但他们已经使用 AI 发布了 20 多个可用的内部工具。 一家医院经营它们。 按照我的标准，他们的理解测试“未通过”，他们系统的某些部分无法逐行解释。

但随后他们说了一句话，改变了一切：“在故意失败的情况下表现出来的行为是赢得信任的另一种形式，这是我唯一可以采用的形式。 造假也更难。”

植入缺陷，观察守卫捕获它们，恢复守卫并观察它们变绿，然后在几秒钟后部署并检查 URL。

他们证明他们可以保持它的活力。

这让我意识到真正的区别不在于谁输入了代码。 这是关于摩擦的。

摩擦力实际上很重要

在我几周前写的早期文章中，我描述了尽管完美地审查了一些逻辑，但仍无法从头开始编写一些逻辑，这不仅仅是技能损失。 这证明我跳过了建立实际理解的摩擦。

当我手工编写代码时，我会实时遇到问题。

我碰壁了。 我的方法行不通。 我重构。 我通过约束和失败发现问题空间。 我做出关于决定的决定，不仅仅是打字，而是在我实际探索过的路径之间进行选择。 这就是我每次手写代码时不知不觉地经历的学习路径，Wii 提醒了我这一点。

当我使用人工智能时，我会描述我想要什么。 我有选择。 我选一个看起来合适的。 我是在策划，而不是在探索。

两者都可以产生好的代码。 但理解的道路却有着根本的不同。

使用手写代码：摩擦、洞察力、更好的下一步决策

人工智能辅助：选择、实施、验证

摩擦就是学习机制。

那么当我说我对手写代码更感到自豪时？ 我对苦难并不浪漫。 我注意到我最引以为豪的代码是我为之奋斗的代码，而手写则迫使我去奋斗。

但这就是这个逻辑的问题

如果摩擦是一种机制，那么摩擦的类型比谁打字更重要。

您可以在以下位置编写人工智能辅助代码：

  • 根据提示进行战斗
  • 批评每个生成的选项
  • 积极重构
  • 撞墙并重新设计

这会产生摩擦，也会建立理解。

相反，您可以手写代码，其中：

  • 通过熟悉的模式自动驾驶
  • 永远不要质疑假设
  • 从 Stack Overflow 复制粘贴
  • 永远不明白为什么它有效

这没有摩擦力，也不会建造任何东西。

所以我的立场的诚实版本并不是“手写代码更好”。 它是：“摩擦可以建立理解，而手写往往会产生摩擦，因为你被迫思考每一行。”

但这是一个偶然的事实，而不是绝对的事实。

令人不安的认识

批评者（守门人，但从现在开始我们将坚持这一点）部分正确，而我在原来的立场上过于慷慨。

不是关于守门本身，不，这仍然是错误的。 但关于趋势：人工智能确实使生成低理解性代码变得更容易。 并不是因为人工智能不好，而是因为消除摩擦正是人工智能所做的事情，而摩擦正是建立理解的基础。

答案不是“少用人工智能”或“从不使用人工智能”。 “如果你使用人工智能来跳过解决问题的过程，无论是代码、故障模式还是维护，你都会构建出更糟糕的系统。

这也适用于人类，但人类有固有的摩擦成本，我​​们会感到无聊，我们讨厌打字，我们会犯错误。 这种摩擦很烦人，但它迫使我们保持参与。

那么什么改变了？

原来的论点没有任何错误。 但我将“理解+责任”视为你可以在最后验证的复选框。

他们不是。

理解不是一种可以检查的财产，而是一个过程，而这个过程需要摩擦。 真正参与解决问题。 你从中吸取教训的错误。

我对手写代码感到更加自豪的原因是因为我以一种难以伪造的方式获得了理解。

这是否意味着每一行都应该手写？ 不，样板就是样板。 有些摩擦只是噪音。

但核心逻辑是什么？ 架构决策？ “理解这段代码”真正重要的地方是什么？ 是的，我想为此而奋斗。

我希望任何重要的运输代码也能得到同样的结果。

不舒服的中间地带

这是我着陆的地方：

对于批评者：您使用了错误的过滤器。 “人工智能或没有人工智能”并不能告诉你任何事情，但你意外地正确地知道有一些真正值得关注的事情，这是人工智能带来的懒惰，而不是工具本身。

致人工智能爱好者：是的，你们的工具太棒了。 但值得一问的是，你是用它来更好地思考还是更少地思考。 直到六个月后您尝试维护代码之前，这些感觉都是一样的。

对我自己来说：我对手写代码的自豪感不是自我，而是合理的。 我打出的每一行并不是某种神奇的独角兽神话中的神行，而是随之而来的摩擦，我所建立的学习。

有时答案需要承认您跳过了，有时这对于日常工作来说很好。 但如果你正在构建一些重要的东西，你应该愿意为之奋斗。

选择战斗地点

我仍然手工编写大量代码。 我仍然每天使用人工智能。 这些不再是矛盾了。

原文是对的：产地并不决定品质。 它忽略的是理解并不是你最后勾选的复选框。 这是你通过摩擦获得的东西。 手写往往会产生这种摩擦。 人工智能倾向于删除它。 两者本质上都没有好坏之分。 两者都是关于如何处理问题的选择。

所以我不是在问“你用过人工智能吗？” 不再了。

我问：你是否为重要的部分而奋斗？

如果该工具为您解答了这个问题，下次出现问题时您就会发现。
